## `auth`

|---|---|
| [`auth add`](#auth-add) | Add credentials for PROVIDER. |
| [`auth login`](#auth-login) | Interactive login for PROVIDER (prompts for all required fields). |

### `auth add`

Add credentials for PROVIDER.

```text
Examples:

  pygeofetch auth add planet --api-key PL_KEY

```


| `--password`, `-p` | text |  | Password (prompted if omitted). |
| `--api-key`, `-k` | text |  | API key (alternative to username/password). |
| `--client-id` | text |  | OAuth2 client ID. |
| `--client-secret` | text |  | OAuth2 client secret. |
| `--token` | text |  | Bearer token. |
| `--store` | one of: keyring, file | `keyring` | Credential storage backend. |

## `search`

Federated search across providers.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`search run`](#search-run) | Search for satellite imagery across one or more providers. |

### `search run`

Search for satellite imagery across one or more providers.

```text
Examples:
  # Basic search with bbox and cloud cover
  pygeofetch search run --bbox "-74,40,-73,41" --cloud-cover 0-20

  # Multiple providers, specific satellite, save GeoJSON
  pygeofetch search run \
      --bbox "-74,40,-73,41" --start-date 2024-01-01 \
      --providers copernicus,aws_earth,planetary_computer \
      --satellites Sentinel-2 --cloud-cover 0-10 \
      --output results.geojson --format geojson

  # AOI from file, CQL2 filter, GeoParquet output
  pygeofetch search run \
      --geometry-file area.geojson \
      --cql2 "eo:cloud_cover < 5 AND platform = 'sentinel-2b'" \
      --format geoparquet --output results.parquet

  # With optical preflight validation (skip cloudy/off-target/wrong-level scenes)
  pygeofetch search run \
      --bbox "-74,40,-73,41" --cloud-cover 0-100 \
      --validate-optical --optical-max-cloud-cover 10 --optical-min-coverage 0.9
```

```text
pygeofetch search run [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bbox`, `-b` | text |  | Bounding box "minx,miny,maxx,maxy". |
| `--geometry-file`, `-g` | path |  | GeoJSON file with search AOI (alternative to --bbox). |
| `--start-date`, `-s` | text |  | Start date YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `--end-date`, `-e` | text |  | End date YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `--cloud-cover`, `-c` | text | `0-100` | Cloud cover range "min-max" e.g. 0-20. |
| `--resolution` | text |  | Resolution range in metres "min-max" e.g. 10-30. |
| `--processing-level` | text |  | Processing level e.g. L2A. |
| `--providers`, `-p` | text |  | Comma-separated provider IDs e.g. usgs,copernicus,planetary_computer. |
| `--satellites` | text |  | Comma-separated satellite names e.g. Sentinel-2,Landsat-8. |
| `--product-type` | text |  | SAR product type e.g. GRD, SLC, GRD-COG. Currently only meaningfully filters Copernicus (OData-based, not STAC) — STAC providers like planetary_computer/element84 offer only pre-processed Sentinel-1 RTC via their collection mapping, not raw GRD/SLC, so this has no effect there regardless of value. |
| `--polarisation` | text |  | SAR polarisation e.g. VV, VH, HH, HV. Same Copernicus-only caveat as --product-type. |
| `--max-results`, `-n` | integer | `100` |  |
| `--sort-by` | one of: datetime, cloud_cover, score, satellite | `datetime` | Sort field. |
| `--sort-order` | one of: asc, desc | `desc` |  |
| `--cql2` | text |  | CQL2 filter expression. |
| `--output`, `-o` | text |  | Save results to this file. |
| `--format` | one of: table, json, stac, geojson, geoparquet, csv, ids | `table` | Output format. |
| `--on-provider-failure` | one of: skip, abort, retry | `skip` | How to handle provider failures. |
| `--timeout` | integer | `60` | Per-provider timeout in seconds. |
| `--no-cache` | flag |  | Bypass result cache. |
| `--validate-optical` | flag |  | Run optical preflight validation (AOI coverage, cloud cover, required bands, processing level, temporal bounds) on results before returning them. Not appropriate for SAR/InSAR searches -- the default required bands are optical band names. |
| `--optical-max-cloud-cover` | float |  | Override the max cloud cover threshold used by --validate-optical (default 20.0). |
| `--optical-min-coverage` | float |  | Override the min AOI coverage ratio used by --validate-optical, 0-1 (default 0.8). |
| `--optical-required-bands` | text |  | Comma-separated required bands for --validate-optical (default B02,B03,B04,B08,SCL). |

## `download`

Download scenes and inspect download history.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`download run`](#download-run) | Download satellite data products from a search results file or scene IDs. |
| [`download status`](#download-status) | Show downloaded files in OUTPUT_DIR. |
| [`download history`](#download-history) | Show download history. |

### `download run`

Download satellite data products from a search results file or scene IDs.

```text
Examples:
  # Basic download
  pygeofetch download run \
      --from-search results.geojson --output ./data/

  # Full-featured download
  pygeofetch download run \
      --from-search results.geojson --output ./data/ \
      --parallel 4 --verify-checksum --resume \
      --bandwidth-limit 10MB --priority high \
      --post-process "unzip,reproject:EPSG:4326,compress:lzw" \
      --notify webhook:https://hooks.slack.com/T01/B01/XYZ \
      --notify email:user@example.com \
      --on-failure skip

  # With optical preflight validation as a final gate before downloading
  pygeofetch download run \
      --from-search results.geojson --output ./data/ \
      --validate-optical --optical-max-cloud-cover 10
```

```text
pygeofetch download run [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--from-search`, `-f` | path |  | GeoJSON results file from `search run --output`. |
| `--scene-ids` | text |  | Comma-separated scene IDs to download. |
| `--output`, `-o` | text | `./pygeofetch_data` | Output directory. |
| `--parallel`, `-p` | integer | `2` | Parallel download workers. |
| `--retry`, `-r` | integer | `3` | Retry attempts per file. |
| `--retry-delay` | float | `5.0` | Base retry delay seconds (exponential backoff). |
| `--verify-checksum` | flag |  | SHA256 checksum verification after download. |
| `--resume` | flag |  | Resume interrupted downloads (default on). |
| `--bandwidth-limit` | text |  | Max bandwidth e.g. 10MB, 5MB (0=unlimited). |
| `--priority` | one of: high, normal, low | `normal` | Download priority. |
| `--notify` | text |  | Notifications: webhook:URL or email:ADDRESS (repeatable). |
| `--post-process` | text |  | Post-process chain e.g. "unzip,reproject:EPSG:4326,compress:lzw". |
| `--on-failure` | one of: skip, abort, retry | `skip` | How to handle individual file failures. |
| `--max-items`, `-n` | integer |  | Limit number of items to download. |
| `--overwrite` | flag |  | Overwrite existing files. |
| `--bands` | text |  | Comma-separated band names to download e.g. "B02,B03,B04" (default: all data assets). |
| `--json` | flag |  | Output results summary as JSON. |
| `--validate-optical` | flag |  | Run optical preflight validation as a final gate before downloading (AOI coverage, cloud cover, required bands, processing level, temporal bounds). Items that fail are never attempted -- a failed result explaining why is returned in their place, same position, so output length always matches input. |
| `--optical-max-cloud-cover` | float |  | Override the max cloud cover threshold used by --validate-optical (default 20.0). |
| `--optical-min-coverage` | float |  | Override the min AOI coverage ratio used by --validate-optical, 0-1 (default 0.8). |
| `--optical-required-bands` | text |  | Comma-separated required bands for --validate-optical (default B02,B03,B04,B08,SCL). |

## `cache`

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`cache stats`](#cache-stats) | Show cache statistics: size, entry count, location, TTL. |

### `cache stats`


### `cache clear`

Delete cache entries with optional filters.

```text
Examples:
  pygeofetch cache clear

```

```text

```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--provider` | text |  | Clear only entries for this provider. |
| `--older-than` | text |  | Clear entries older than (e.g. 7d, 24h). |
| `--dry-run` | flag |  | Show what would be removed without deleting. |
| `--yes` | flag |  | Confirm the action without prompting. |

### `cache ttl`

Show or set cache TTL. Usage: ttl show | ttl set SECONDS

```text

```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `ACTION` | required |
| `SECONDS` | optional |

### `cache location`

Show the cache directory path.

```text

```

### `cache prune`

Remove oldest cache entries to stay under max-size.

```text

```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--max-size` | text | `1GB` | Prune oldest entries until cache is below this size (e.g. 500MB, 2GB). |

## `preprocess`

Clip, reproject, mask, correct and mosaic rasters.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`preprocess clip`](#preprocess-clip) | Clip raster to bounding box or polygon geometry. |
| [`preprocess reproject`](#preprocess-reproject) | Reproject raster to a new CRS (e.g. EPSG:4326, EPSG:32618). |
| [`preprocess resample`](#preprocess-resample) | Resample raster to different spatial resolution. |
| [`preprocess cloud-mask`](#preprocess-cloud-mask) | Apply cloud masking to set cloud pixels to NoData. |
| [`preprocess cloud-fill`](#preprocess-cloud-fill) | Fill cloud gaps using a time series of auxiliary scenes. |
| [`preprocess atmos`](#preprocess-atmos) | Atmospheric correction (DOS1, DOS2, Sen2Cor, FLAASH, 6S, iCOR). |
| [`preprocess topo-correct`](#preprocess-topo-correct) | Topographic correction using a DEM (cosine, Minnaert, C-correction). |
| [`preprocess pansharpen`](#preprocess-pansharpen) | Pan-sharpen multispectral using panchromatic band. |
| [`preprocess mosaic`](#preprocess-mosaic) | Merge multiple rasters into a seamless mosaic. |
| [`preprocess composite`](#preprocess-composite) | Create multi-temporal composite (median, mean, max, min, best-pixel). |
| [`preprocess tile`](#preprocess-tile) | Split large raster into overlapping tiles for AI inference. |

### `preprocess clip`

Clip raster to bounding box or polygon geometry.

```text
pygeofetch preprocess clip [OPTIONS] INPUT
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `INPUT` | required |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bbox`, `-b` | text |  | "minx,miny,maxx,maxy" |
| `--geometry`, `-g` | path |  |  |
| `--output`, `-o` | text |  |  |
| `--all-touched` | flag |  |  |

## `index`

Spectral indices and band arithmetic.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`index ndvi`](#index-ndvi) | NDVI — Normalized Difference Vegetation Index. Range: -1 to +1. Vegetation > 0.3. |
| [`index ndre`](#index-ndre) | NDRE — Normalized Difference Red Edge Index. Range: -1 to +1. |
| [`index evi`](#index-evi) | EVI — Enhanced Vegetation Index. Better than NDVI in high-biomass areas. |
| [`index savi`](#index-savi) | SAVI — Soil Adjusted Vegetation Index. Reduces soil brightness influence. |
| [`index ndwi`](#index-ndwi) | NDWI — Normalized Difference Water Index. Water > 0. |
| [`index mndwi`](#index-mndwi) | MNDWI — Modified NDWI. Better separation of water from built-up areas. |
| [`index ndbi`](#index-ndbi) | NDBI — Normalized Difference Built-up Index. Urban > 0. |
| [`index ndsi`](#index-ndsi) | NDSI — Snow Index. Snow > 0.4. |
| [`index ndmi`](#index-ndmi) | NDMI — Moisture Index. Sensitive to canopy water content. |
| [`index nbr`](#index-nbr) | NBR — Normalized Burn Ratio. Use dNBR for burn severity. |
| [`index dnbr`](#index-dnbr) | dNBR — Differenced Burn Ratio. Range: >0.66 high severity, <-0.25 regrowth. |
| [`index tct`](#index-tct) | Tasseled Cap Transformation — Brightness, Greenness, Wetness (3-band output). |
| [`index pca`](#index-pca) | PCA — Principal Component Analysis. Reduces dimensionality of multi-band data. |
| [`index texture`](#index-texture) | GLCM Texture — contrast, homogeneity, energy, correlation, dissimilarity, ASM. |
| [`index lst`](#index-lst) | Land Surface Temperature from thermal band. Output: Band1=Kelvin, Band2=Celsius. |
| [`index albedo`](#index-albedo) | Surface albedo from narrowband to broadband conversion (Liang 2001). |
| [`index band-math`](#index-band-math) | Arbitrary band arithmetic. Example: --expr '(B[1]-B[0])/(B[1]+B[0])'. |
| [`index stack`](#index-stack) | Stack single-band rasters into a multi-band GeoTIFF. |

### `index ndvi`

NDVI — Normalized Difference Vegetation Index. Range: -1 to +1. Vegetation > 0.3.

```text
Pass the SAME path to --red and --nir to auto-detect both bands from
one merged multi-band image (e.g. a drone orthomosaic), using its
real, embedded band descriptions.
```

```text
pygeofetch index ndvi [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--red` | path | required | Red band (e.g. B04.tif) |
| `--nir` | path | required | NIR band (e.g. B08.tif) |
| `--output`, `-o` | text |  |  |
| `--chunked` | flag |  | Process in memory-safe tiles for large rasters (e.g. drone orthomosaics) that exceed available RAM or the 4GB GeoTIFF limit. |
| `--tile-size` | integer | `1024` | Tile edge length in pixels when --chunked is set. |
| `--geometry-crs` | text | `EPSG:4326` | CRS of --bbox/--geometry coordinates. |
| `--geometry` | path |  | Clip the result to a GeoJSON file's geometry instead of a bbox. |
| `--bbox` | text |  | Clip the result to minx,miny,maxx,maxy (comma-separated). |

### `index ndre`

NDRE — Normalized Difference Red Edge Index. Range: -1 to +1.

```text
Less prone to saturation than NDVI in dense canopy -- useful for
crop stress and chlorophyll monitoring from drone multispectral
sensors. Pass the SAME path to --rededge and --nir to auto-detect
both bands from one merged multi-band image.
```

```text
pygeofetch index ndre [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--rededge` | path | required | Red edge band |
| `--nir` | path | required | NIR band |
| `--output`, `-o` | text |  |  |
| `--chunked` | flag |  | Process in memory-safe tiles for large rasters that exceed available RAM or the 4GB GeoTIFF limit. |
| `--tile-size` | integer | `1024` | Tile edge length in pixels when --chunked is set. |
| `--geometry-crs` | text | `EPSG:4326` | CRS of --bbox/--geometry coordinates. |
| `--geometry` | path |  | Clip the result to a GeoJSON file's geometry instead of a bbox. |
| `--bbox` | text |  | Clip the result to minx,miny,maxx,maxy (comma-separated). |

## `classify`

Unsupervised and supervised classification.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`classify kmeans`](#classify-kmeans) | Unsupervised K-means clustering. No training data needed. |
| [`classify train`](#classify-train) | Train a supervised classifier from labeled vector training samples. |
| [`classify predict`](#classify-predict) | Apply a trained model to a real raster stack, producing a classification map. |

### `classify kmeans`

Unsupervised K-means clustering. No training data needed.

```text
Example: pygeofetch classify kmeans B02.tif B03.tif B04.tif B08.tif -k 5
```

```text
pygeofetch classify kmeans [OPTIONS] [INPUTS]...
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `INPUTS` | optional |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--clusters`, `-k` | integer | `5` | Number of clusters. |
| `--output`, `-o` | text |  |  |
| `--random-state` | integer | `42` |  |

### `classify train`

Train a supervised classifier from labeled vector training samples.

```text
Example: pygeofetch classify train B02.tif B03.tif B04.tif B08.tif
          --training-data samples.geojson --class-field land_cover -o model.joblib
```

```text
pygeofetch classify train [OPTIONS] [INPUTS]...
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `INPUTS` | optional |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--training-data` | path | required | Vector file (GeoJSON/Shapefile) with labeled training geometries. |
| `--class-field` | text | required | Attribute column holding the real class label. |
| `--output-model`, `-o` | text | required | Where to save the trained model. |
| `--model-type` | one of: random_forest, svm | `random_forest` |  |
| `--n-estimators` | integer | `100` | Random Forest tree count. |
| `--test-size` | float | `0.2` | Fraction of samples held out for real accuracy reporting. |

### `classify predict`

Apply a trained model to a real raster stack, producing a classification map.

```text
Example: pygeofetch classify predict B02.tif B03.tif B04.tif B08.tif -m model.joblib
```

```text
pygeofetch classify predict [OPTIONS] [INPUTS]...
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `INPUTS` | optional |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--model`, `-m` | path | required | A model trained via 'classify train'. |
| `--output`, `-o` | text |  |  |

## `post`

Vector and raster post-processing.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`post vectorize`](#post-vectorize) | Convert raster to vector polygons (polygonize). |
| [`post smooth`](#post-smooth) | Smooth/simplify vector geometries (Douglas-Peucker or buffer-unbuffer). |
| [`post regularize`](#post-regularize) | Regularize (orthogonalize) building footprints or polygons. |
| [`post zonal-stats`](#post-zonal-stats) | Compute zonal statistics for each polygon zone. |
| [`post buffer`](#post-buffer) | Add buffer around vector geometries. |
| [`post centroids`](#post-centroids) | Extract centroid points from polygons. |
| [`post geometry-metrics`](#post-geometry-metrics) | Add area, perimeter, and compactness columns to vector file. |
| [`post compress`](#post-compress) | Apply lossless compression to a GeoTIFF. |
| [`post cog`](#post-cog) | Convert to Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) with internal tiling and overviews. |
| [`post overlay`](#post-overlay) | Real polygon overlay between two vector layers. |
| [`post dissolve`](#post-dissolve) | Merge polygons sharing the same attribute value into single geometries. |
| [`post spatial-join`](#post-spatial-join) | Attach attributes from one vector layer to another by real spatial relationship. |

### `post vectorize`

Convert raster to vector polygons (polygonize).

```text
pygeofetch post vectorize [OPTIONS] INPUT
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `INPUT` | required |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--output`, `-o` | text |  |  |
| `--band`, `-b` | integer | `1` |  |
| `--threshold`, `-t` | float |  | Binary threshold before vectorizing. |
| `--format`, `-f` | one of: geojson, gpkg, shp | `geojson` |  |
| `--min-area` | float |  | Minimum polygon area to keep (CRS units²). |

### `post spatial-join`

Attach attributes from one vector layer to another by real spatial relationship.

```text
Example: pygeofetch post spatial-join points.geojson zones.geojson -o joined.geojson --predicate within
```

```text
pygeofetch post spatial-join [OPTIONS] LEFT RIGHT
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `LEFT` | required |
| `RIGHT` | required |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--output`, `-o` | text | required |  |
| `--how` | one of: inner, left, right | `inner` |  |
| `--predicate` | one of: intersects, contains, within, touches, crosses, overlaps | `intersects` |  |

## `optical`

Optical pixel-offset tracking.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`optical offset-track`](#optical-offset-track) | Measure 2D ground displacement between two optical scenes via |

### `optical offset-track`

Measure 2D ground displacement between two optical scenes via image correlation.

```text
Examples:
  # Basic: two co-registered scenes, real cloud masking via SCL
  pygeofetch optical offset-track \
      --ref before.tif --sec after.tif \
      --cloud-mask before_SCL.tif \
      --output displacement.tif

  # Mining-scale displacement, larger search window
  pygeofetch optical offset-track \
      --ref jan.tif --sec jun.tif \
      --window-size 96 --step-size 24 \
      --output mine_displacement.tif
```

```text
pygeofetch optical offset-track [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ref` | path | required | Reference-date raster. |
| `--sec` | path | required | Secondary-date raster. |
| `--output`, `-o` | path | required | Output GeoTIFF (dx/dy/snr, 3 bands). |
| `--band` | integer | `1` | 1-based band index to correlate. |
| `--window-size` | integer | `64` | Search window size, pixels. |
| `--step-size` | integer | `16` | Spacing between window centers, pixels. |
| `--chip-size` | integer |  | Reference template size, pixels. Default: window-size // 2. |
| `--snr-threshold` | float | `3.0` | Minimum SNR to mark a window reliable. |
| `--cloud-mask` | path |  | Real Sentinel-2 SCL raster, already aligned to --ref. |
| `--water-mask-threshold` | float |  | Mask pixels where NDWI exceeds this value (needs --green-band/--nir-band). |
| `--green-band` | integer |  | 1-based green band index, for --water-mask-threshold. |
| `--nir-band` | integer |  | 1-based NIR band index, for --water-mask-threshold. |

## `stream`

Windowed COG reads and cloud-native format conversion.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`stream cog-window`](#stream-cog-window) | Read a real, spatial window from a remote COG without downloading the whole file. |
| [`stream to-geoparquet`](#stream-to-geoparquet) | Convert any real vector file to GeoParquet. |
| [`stream to-zarr`](#stream-to-zarr) | Convert a real GeoTIFF to a chunked Zarr store. |
| [`stream zarr-to-tif`](#stream-zarr-to-tif) | Convert a real Zarr store (written with real geo metadata) back to GeoTIFF. |
| [`stream chunked-process`](#stream-chunked-process) | Process a large raster in real, memory-safe, overlap-aware tiles. |

### `stream cog-window`

Read a real, spatial window from a remote COG without downloading the whole file.

```text
Example: pygeofetch stream cog-window https://example.com/scene.tif \
         --bbox 36.7,-1.4,36.9,-1.2 -o window.tif
```

```text
pygeofetch stream cog-window [OPTIONS] URL
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `URL` | required |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bbox` | text | required | min_lon,min_lat,max_lon,max_lat |
| `--bbox-crs` | text | `EPSG:4326` |  |
| `--bands` | text |  | Comma-separated 1-based band indices. Default: all real bands. |
| `--output`, `-o` | text | required | Output GeoTIFF path for the real, windowed result. |
| `--no-range-check` | flag |  | Skip the real, honest pre-flight range-request support check. |

### `stream to-geoparquet`

Convert any real vector file to GeoParquet.

```text
Example: pygeofetch stream to-geoparquet parcels.geojson -o parcels.parquet
```

```text
pygeofetch stream to-geoparquet [OPTIONS] INPUT_VECTOR
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `INPUT_VECTOR` | required |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--output`, `-o` | text | required |  |

### `stream to-zarr`

Convert a real GeoTIFF to a chunked Zarr store.

```text
Example: pygeofetch stream to-zarr velocity.tif -o velocity.zarr --chunks 512,512
```

```text
pygeofetch stream to-zarr [OPTIONS] INPUT_RASTER
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `INPUT_RASTER` | required |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--output`, `-o` | text | required | Output .zarr store directory. |
| `--chunks` | text |  | Comma-separated chunk shape, e.g. 512,512. Default: real, automatic. |
| `--compressor` | one of: zstd, lz4, gzip, zlib, none | `zstd` |  |

### `stream zarr-to-tif`

Convert a real Zarr store (written with real geo metadata) back to GeoTIFF.

```text
Example: pygeofetch stream zarr-to-tif velocity.zarr -o velocity.tif
```

```text
pygeofetch stream zarr-to-tif [OPTIONS] INPUT_ZARR
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `INPUT_ZARR` | required |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--output`, `-o` | text | required |  |

### `stream chunked-process`

Process a large raster in real, memory-safe, overlap-aware tiles.

```text
B[0], B[1], ... refer to each input in order. numpy is available as
np, and scipy.ndimage's uniform_filter/median_filter/generic_filter
are available directly by name for real neighborhood operations.

Examples:


  # Pixel-independent (overlap=0 is fine)
  pygeofetch stream chunked-process red.tif nir.tif \
      -e "(B[1]-B[0])/(B[1]+B[0]+1e-6)" -o ndvi.tif


  # Real neighborhood operation (needs overlap >= window_size // 2)
  pygeofetch stream chunked-process large_raster.tif \
      -e "uniform_filter(B[0], size=3, mode='nearest')" \
      --overlap 1 -o smoothed.tif
```

```text
pygeofetch stream chunked-process [OPTIONS] [INPUTS]...
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `INPUTS` | optional |

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--expression`, `-e` | text | required | Python expression over tile arrays, e.g. "(B[1]-B[0])/(B[1]+B[0]+1e-6)" for pixel-independent math, or "uniform_filter(B[0], size=3)" for a real neighborhood filter. |
| `--tile-size` | integer | `1024` |  |
| `--overlap` | integer | `0` | Real pixel margin for neighborhood operations -- 0 for pixel-independent math. |
| `--output-format` | one of: cog, zarr | `cog` |  |
| `--output`, `-o` | text | required |  |

## `config`

Read and modify configuration.

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`config show`](#config-show) | Show the effective configuration (all layers merged). |
| [`config get`](#config-get) | Get a single configuration value by dotted KEY path. |
| [`config set`](#config-set) | Set a configuration value in the user config file. |
| [`config path`](#config-path) | Show the location of configuration files. |
| [`config reset`](#config-reset) | Remove the user configuration file, restoring defaults. |

### `config show`

Show the effective configuration (all layers merged).

```text
pygeofetch config show [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--json` | flag |  | Output as JSON. |

### `config get`

Get a single configuration value by dotted KEY path.

```text
Example:
  pygeofetch config get download.parallel
```

```text
pygeofetch config get [OPTIONS] KEY
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `KEY` | required |

### `config set`

Set a configuration value in the user config file.

```text
The value is cast to int/float/bool if it looks like one; otherwise stored as string.


Example:
  pygeofetch config set download.parallel 4
  pygeofetch config set cache.ttl_seconds 7200
```

```text
pygeofetch config set [OPTIONS] KEY VALUE
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `KEY` | required |
| `VALUE` | required |

### `config path`

Show the location of configuration files.

```text
pygeofetch config path [OPTIONS]
```

### `config reset`

Remove the user configuration file, restoring defaults.

```text
pygeofetch config reset [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--yes` | flag |  | Confirm the action without prompting. |

### `status`

```text
Displays authenticated providers with quota, cache statistics, active
downloads, scheduled pipelines, and system information.
```


|---|---|---|---|
| `--json` | flag |  | Output as JSON. |

```text
Checks: Python version, required packages, config directory, keyring,
network connectivity to provider endpoints.
```


### `assess-feasibility`

Assess InSAR feasibility for an AOI before downloading anything.

```text
Example: pygeofetch assess-feasibility --bbox 18.85,50.15,19.15,50.35 \
         --start-date 2016-01-01 --end-date 2021-06-30

Reports the real, largest temporally-connected component per track
-- an honest upper bound, not a guarantee InSAR will work.
```

```text
pygeofetch assess-feasibility [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bbox` | text | required | min_lon,min_lat,max_lon,max_lat |
| `--start-date` | text | required |  |
| `--end-date` | text | required |  |
| `--max-temporal-baseline` | integer | `72` |  |
| `--deep-check` | flag |  | Also run real, live burst-sync screening on the best track (costs real network calls). |
